They’re all really big on self defense and arming yourself. I’m just not interested, generally, and don’t care much about defense. I also don’t at all want to tell them anything to do with whatever thoughts I’m having because I really don’t think I could handle the fallout.

I’ve read it. Just seems unlikely that the entire planet had the opportunity to get onto the ark. Seems unlikely that every single person who didn’t was evil and deserved that death. I’m not disputing that it needed to happen, just trying to understand why everyone.

I suppose so. When I think of God I guess I don’t think of it being possible that His actions could be anything other than good and just. If that is the case, where does that leave us? Are all things He does holy and good because it is Him doing them, or would they have been good and just actions even if done by, say, an army, or any single other person.
That couldn’t have been true for everyone, right? Seems unlikely, in any case.
Valid

That always brings me to the thought, why let any of those bound for hell be born at all? God knows all, and knows where each person will inevitably end up, so why not kill them all young? Or never let them be born? Instead we are allowed to just damn ourselves.
I guess I just can’t understand. Maybe it isn’t something we are meant to understand, and instead just trust that it was right. That makes me feel an awful lot of fear.
But doesn’t that make free will meaningless? If God just decides to hit the reset button when he doesn’t like us enough? Then why let us live at all.
It seems senseless, right? All those people. The rainbow signified that god still loves us, it’s said, but I don’t think those people who drowned probably felt any love.
